findings.title: Materials' 119% earnings hope is a 54% multiple bet
findings.body: Materials' trailing P/E sits at the 93rd percentile of its five-year range, yet the forward multiple is only at the 44th. The market is underwriting 119 percent earnings growth, a bet that the current earnings trough is temporary and that the 54 percent compression is justified.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' one-month slide breaks its rich streak
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile dropped 33 points in a month, even as the trailing multiple remains at the 84th percentile. That 47-point gap between lenses suggests the market is rapidly repricing expectations for earnings growth, not just a valuation reset.

findings.title: Utilities' cheapness is a five-year anomaly
findings.body: Utilities' forward P/E percentile fell 28 points in a month to the 19th, with the trailing multiple at the 6th percentile. This is a sector at the bottom of its own valuation range, a position that has historically been rare for a defensive group.
